title: The CIE 99 color evaluation samples
description: The 99 samples the CIE chose from over 100,000 measured spectra to cover object colors evenly and to vary in spectrum: things from nature, skin, textiles, paints, plastics, print and color systems. Made for judging how lights render colors (CIE 224, and the CES of ANSI/IES TM-30-18); here, a small, balanced test set.
source: CIE 224:2017, CIE 2017 Colour Fidelity Index for accurate scientific use: spectral radiance factors of the 99 test samples (5 nm), the color evaluation samples (CES) of ANSI/IES TM-30-18.
license: CC BY-SA 4.0 (International Commission on Illumination, CIE)
changes: Put in this layout and stored to 1/10000.

title: Natural objects measured in Japan
description: 359 natural objects: 200 flowers, 113 leaves, 23 fruits, 6 vegetables, 8 pieces of bark and 9 stones, measured outdoors and in the laboratory by Morimoto, Zhang, Fukuda and Uchikawa. Spectra of the kind made by living things, unlike those of paints and inks.
source: Morimoto T, Zhang C, Fukuda K, Uchikawa K. Spectral dataset of daylights and surface properties of natural objects measured in Japan (version 1.2). Zenodo, 2021.
changes: Put in this layout and stored to 1/10000.

title: The Munsell soil color chart
description: The 443 chips of the Munsell soil color chart (2009 edition): its soil, gley, neutral and white pages. Browns, yellows and grays of low chroma, made of pigments.
source: Munsell soil color chart: a spectral reflectance dataset (version 1.1). Zenodo, 2023.
instrument: Konica Minolta CS-2000 spectroradiometer, tungsten lamp
changes: Sampled every 5 nm from 1 nm, put in this layout and stored to 1/10000.

title: Human skin (NIST)
description: The skin of 100 people, each the average of three measurements, from the National Institute of Standards and Technology. Few hues, but colors that people judge closely.
source: Cooksey C, Allen D, Tsai B. Reference Data Set of Human Skin Reflectance. J Res NIST 122:26, 2017. Data: NIST, version 3.
changes: The average of each person's three spectra, resampled from 3 nm to 5 nm, 380 to 780 nm only, stored to 1/10000.

title: The Preferred Memory Colour Chart (PMCC)
description: The 30 patches of a PMCC, a printed chart of the colors people remember and prefer: skin of four ethnic groups, foods, grass, sky and flowers, then the four unitary hues, magenta, cyan and six neutrals. Colors people judge by memory, as printed.
source: The Preferred Memory Colour Chart (M. R. Luo, "The new preferred memory color (PMC) chart," Color Research & Application 49(6), 564-576, 2024, DOI 10.1002/col.22940), measured by Maxim W. Derhak from 380 to 730 nm at 10 nm.
license: BSD 3-Clause, with the wlab package (the measurements are its own data)
changes: Interpolated to 5 nm, the 730 nm value held to 780 nm, stored to 1/10000.
